从囚犯到侦探，维多克的人生几次转弯；1840 年前后，他曾住在这座拱廊里。: From prisoner to detective, Vidocq’s life took several turns. Around 1840, this arcade was his address.
维多克做过囚犯，也为巴黎警察工作，后来经营私人侦探机构。他的经历常被联系到巴尔扎: Vidocq had been a prisoner, worked for the Paris police and later ran a private detective agency. His life is often linked to Balzac’s Vautrin, although a fictional character is never simply a copy of one person. Look for the staircase at number 13: the City of Paris places his apartment above it around 1840. Beneath the glass roof, shops occupied the ground floor while a life fit for a novel unfolded upstairs.
这家书店的过去，还藏着一份把英语新闻带到巴黎的报纸。: Behind this bookshop lies the story of a newspaper that brought English-language news to Paris.
加利尼亚尼家族的事业不只有卖书，也包括出版与报纸。《加利尼亚尼信使报》创办于 1: The Galignani family’s business combined bookselling, publishing and newspapers. Founded in 1814, Galignani’s Messenger carried material from British newspapers alongside news from elsewhere for English-speaking residents and travellers in Europe. The shop offers a glimpse of an older network across languages: books and newspapers helped people abroad stay connected. The bookshop moved to its present Rue de Rivoli address in 1856, so the newspaper’s beginnings should not be placed inside today’s premises.
百货公司创始人留下的收藏，后来搬进了玛黑区一座更古老的宅邸。: A department-store founder’s collection eventually found a home in an older Marais townhouse.
科尼亚克与热夫妇在 1900 至 1927 年间收藏了大量十八世纪艺术品。科尼亚: Between 1900 and 1927, Ernest Cognacq and Marie-Louise Jay assembled a collection of eighteenth-century art. Bequeathed to Paris after Cognacq’s death, it became a museum on Boulevard des Capucines in 1929. The Hôtel Donon has housed it since 1990; this is not the couple’s former home. Among the furniture, paintings and small treasures, consider how a department store serving the public and a private taste for the eighteenth century could emerge from the same lives.
绿色书箱看起来随意，背后却有一段关于书、街道与城市管理的历史。: The green book boxes look informal, but their story involves books, streets and city rules.
沿塞纳河展开的绿色书箱，把散步与翻书放在同一段路上。流动书贩逐渐获得固定摊位，箱: Along the Seine, green boxes bring browsing and strolling together. Itinerant booksellers gradually gained fixed pitches, with the placement of boxes and trading shaped by city rules. Their cultural appeal belongs to the wider riverside landscape. The UNESCO property inscribed in 1991 is Paris, Banks of the Seine; the bookstalls did not receive a separate World Heritage designation. Pause at an open box to see books, prints and postcards bring different periods together. Which stalls are open varies on the day.
今天人们上屋顶看巴黎，1919 年，韦德里纳却把一架飞机降落在这里。: Today visitors come to the roof for the view. In 1919, Védrines arrived by aeroplane.
1919 年 1 月 19 日，朱尔·韦德里纳驾驶 Caudron G.3 飞机: On 19 January 1919, Jules Védrines landed a Caudron G.3 on the roof of Galeries Lafayette, taking up the store’s earlier prize challenge. The store’s historical account describes a terrace roughly 28 metres long and 12 metres wide. The feat became part of both aviation and retail publicity history. Looking across the rooftops, imagine the judgement it required, while remembering that today’s viewing terrace differs from the roof as it was then.

经营者用“十九世纪的幸存者”形容它；这是一种看待餐厅历史的说法。: Its operator describes it as a survivor of the nineteenth century: one way of framing the restaurant’s history.
格兰大道的 Chartier 开业于 1896 年。经营者 Christophe: The Grands Boulevards Chartier opened in 1896. Operator Christophe Joulie has described it as the last surviving nineteenth-century bouillon. That is an operator’s framing, rather than a conclusion established by surveying every Paris restaurant. What visitors can see directly is the dining room and the tradition of an accessible meal in an old restaurant. The same brand’s Montparnasse restaurant is a different location with its own opening and name changes.
一杯血腥玛丽，几种起源说: One Bloody Mary, Several Origin Stories
谁先把番茄汁、伏特加和调料放在一起？巴黎与纽约留下了不同版本。: Who first combined tomato juice, vodka and seasoning? Paris and New York preserve different accounts.
Harry’s 的历史叙述把血腥玛丽的起源联系到调酒师 Fernand Peti: Harry’s account connects the Bloody Mary to bartender Fernand Petiot and Paris in the 1920s. New York bar traditions and later interviews also concern refinements to the recipe, the name Red Snapper and George Jessel’s claim about the basic mixture. These accounts may describe different steps: mixing vodka and tomato juice, adding seasoning, naming and popularising the drink. At the bar, the interesting story is how a cocktail took shape, rather than a settled certificate of invention.
起源叙述涉及经营方回忆和后来的访谈，不能据此确定唯一发明人、地点或年份。: The accounts include operators’ recollections and later interviews; they do not establish a single inventor, location or year.

把休息时望见的屋顶，变成聚会的地方: Turning a Rooftop into a Meeting Place
2013 年开业的 Le Perchoir，把一处高楼上的空间变成了人们专程寻找: Opened in 2013, Le Perchoir turned an elevated space into a terrace people sought out.
关于 Le Perchoir 的起步，创始人的访谈讲到一个很日常的念头：工作休息: In interviews about Le Perchoir’s beginnings, its founders describe an everyday thought: looking up during work breaks and wondering what the space could become. It developed into a place to meet over a drink and look across the city. Hard to see from the street, the terrace makes finding the entrance and heading upstairs part of the experience. It contributed to the popularity of Paris rooftop bars, without needing a claim to have been the first or to have started the entire trend.

Abdelkader Mesli 曾在巴黎大清真寺任职，后来在波尔多参与抵抗活动: Abdelkader Mesli served at the Grande Mosquée de Paris and later took part in resistance activities in Bordeaux. Arrested in 1944 and deported to a concentration camp, he survived. The forecourt now bears his name. Accounts of help given to persecuted people during the occupation need to be read separately: an individual’s resistance work, allegations in contemporary documents and claims of larger rescue operations require different evidence. Learning his name and following the sources offers a more grounded way into this memorial’s history.
清真寺的救援故事：记忆与档案之间: Rescue Stories at the Mosque: Memory and Archives
一些故事经由口述和电影广为流传；具体人数与行动细节，仍需档案印证。: Oral accounts and films have spread these stories; numbers and operational details still require archival evidence.
巴黎大清真寺与战时救援有关的故事，经由口述、报道和电影传播。其中，歌手 Sali: Stories connecting the Grande Mosquée de Paris with wartime rescue have circulated through oral accounts, reporting and film. Accounts of help given to singer Salim Halali and claims that hundreds of Jewish children were hidden in a basement should not be merged into one verified event. Whether individual assistance occurred, who provided it and how extensive it was are separate questions. Research disputes the completeness of the evidence and some details: widespread retelling does not establish a headcount, while insufficient evidence is not the same as disproof.
救援规模与具体叙述仍有证据争议，此处不采用未经核实的人数。: Evidence about the scale and details of rescue remains contested; no unverified headcount is adopted here.
